summary:
Artemis Flight Academy is A web-based astronaut training platform. It has a 6-DOF 3D/VR orbital docking simulator, lunar and Martian outpost engineering simulations, real-time multiplayer mission telemetry, encrypted flight credentials that record a trainee’s progress, and AI analytics that find gaps in each trainee’s skills.

How does it address the challenge
Artemis and future Moon-to-Mars missions need a larger, better-prepared workforce, but astronaut-level training is expensive and reachable by very few people. Artemis Flight Academy puts mission-style training (docking, habitat engineering, teamwork under telemetry) in any browser. It turns NASA’s exploration goals into hands-on practice for students and aspiring space professionals.

 Why is it important
Artemis and Mars exploration will need engineers, pilots, and mission specialists from many countries, not only those near NASA centers. Many talented learners, especially in regions like Africa, have no access to simulators or space-training programs. This project lowers that barrier with a free, browser-based platform.
details:
Trainees sign in and get an encrypted flight credential that stores their progress.
They pick a mission module: orbital docking (3D or VR, with full six-degree-of-freedom control), or lunar and Martian outpost engineering.
Multiplayer mode shares real-time telemetry, so crews can work together on a mission.
The AI analytics engine reviews performance, finds weak areas (such as fuel use, approach speed, or resource planning), and recommends what to practice next.


Widen access to space-training experience for students and the public.
Prepare the next generation of the Artemis workforce.
Inspire interest in STEM and space careers.
Give learners a measurable skill record they can build on.

HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; Three.js / WebGL for 3D; WebXR for VR; WebSockets (or similar) for real-time multiplayer; Web Crypto API for encrypted credentials; an AI/analytics layer for gap analysis; Netlify for hosting; GitHub for version control.

It combines several things that are usually separate: realistic docking physics, Moon and Mars engineering, multiplayer teamwork, VR, and personalized AI coaching. Credentials are encrypted and portable, so learners own their training record. It treats training as a mission, not a lesson, which makes it engaging for young people.


Accessibility: it runs in a browser, with no expensive hardware needed, and VR is optional.
Realism vs. usability: accurate 6-DOF mechanics that beginners can still learn.
Security and privacy: encrypted credentials protect user data.
Collaboration: real-time telemetry supports crew-style training.
Scalability and performance: it should run smoothly on low-end devices and slow connections.
Inclusivity: it is designed for learners worldwide.
